title: Burst demultiplexing cost & latency scenarios — cribsheet
content:
Quick overview

Purpose: short, shareable bench cribsheet comparing demultiplexing strategies for handling microbursts. Intended for product and infra folks deciding tradeoffs for a tiered SLA rollout. This is a working draft — notes, quick ASCII charts, and action items.

High-level summary (TL;DR)
- We tested 4 runtime policies under a synthetic microburst workload that mimics conversational chat spikes (short bursts of many concurrent short requests).
- Soft-demux (fast reallocation of slots on burst detection) reduces p99 tail by ~40–50% versus pure shared multiplexing at modest cost increase (~10–15%).
- Hard-demux (dedicated slot per session during burst) gives the best tail but increases $/1M tokens materially; should be reserved for premium tenants or hard-SLA routes.
- Prewarm combined with soft-demux gives similar tail to hard-demux for short bursts but wastes capacity on long sustained loads.

Experiment setup (concise)
- Model: rdx-7B-opt (cpu/gpu kernel mix, quantized runtime identical configs).
- Hardware: single GVE-GPU pool (A100-equivalent), 48GB GPU, unified runtime.
- Workload: baseline steady traffic + injected microbursts (10s bursts every 60s), request shape: 12 tokens prompt + average 40 tokens generation; 75% short (<=100 tokens), 25% long (>=400 tokens) tail mix.
- Session profile: 70% single-shot, 30% conversational (session affinity).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec sustained, cost extrapolated to $/1M tokens using current unit costs.
- Notes: caching disabled (we wanted pure routing/slot effects). All runs ran for 30 minutes; stable numbers from 20–30 minute window used.

Policies tested
- shared-multiplex: default multiplexing, work-stealing scheduler, no per-session isolation.
- soft-demux: monitor short-term load per virtual client; upon detection allocate a temporary dedicated worker for the session for the burst window (ttl 12s); reclaims when idle.
- hard-demux: always assign a dedicated worker (virtual slot) to session for its lifetime (session pinning).
- prewarm-boost: keep a small warm pool that can be immediately assigned (combines with any of the above; in tests we used prewarm+soft-demux).

Numeric snapshot (representative numbers)
Policy | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/sec | $/1M tokens
---------------------------------------------------------------------
shared-multiplex | 118 | 228 | 356 | 962 | 8,200 | 17.9
soft-demux       | 107 | 186 | 252 | 508 | 7,500 | 20.4
hard-demux       | 92  | 142 | 212 | 376 | 6,100 | 27.9
prewarm+soft     | 88  | 136 | 206 | 392 | 6,250 | 28.6

Interpretation of the table
- Tail improvement: moving from shared-multiplex -> soft-demux drops p99 by roughly 45% (962 -> 508 ms). Big wins for minimal complexity.
- Cost: soft-demux increases dollars per token by ~14% compared to shared (from 17.9 -> 20.4) due to reserved micro-slots during bursts and some allocation churn.
- Hard-demux shows the classic tail vs efficiency tradeoff: best p99 but ~55% higher $/token vs shared. Useful where p99 is prioritized above cost.
- Prewarm gives tail similar to hard-demux for short bursts but shows increased cost because warm slots sit idle between bursts. Not great for irregular bursts.

ASCII timeline (single 60s window, burst at t=20s lasting 10s):
Time(s):   0    5   10   15   20   25   30   35   40   45   50   55   60
shared-mux: 120 130 125 140 220 420 740 360 210 150 130 122 118
soft-demux: 115 118 121 125 140 180 230 160 132 122 118 116 115
hard-demux: 100 102 99  101 106 110 118 105 101 100 99  98  96
(prewarm+soft similar to hard during 20-35s, but baseline slightly higher due to prewarm costs)

ASCII sparkline — p99 by policy (normalized visual):
shared-multiplex: ▁▁▂▂▃▅▇
soft-demux:      ▁▁▁▁▂▃▅
hard-demux:      ▁▁▁▁▁▁▂

Key observations / qualitative notes
- Soft-demux latency drop is driven by avoiding queue head-of-line blocking: small bursts can be diverted to a freshly allocated worker instead of waiting behind long-running requests on multiplexed workers.
- The cost delta for soft-demux arises primarily from transient slot allocation and slightly lower aggregate packing efficiency. There is also a small increase in kernel warmup churn but not significant for the short bursts tested.
- Hard-demux is the most predictable for p99 but reduces packing density and increases instance-hours. It also complicates tenant isolation accounting (billing and chargeback).
- Prewarm is effective when bursts are frequent and predictable (low duty cycle). For irregular bursts it wastes capacity.

Recommended rollout heuristics (practical)
1) Default: keep shared-multiplex for free-tier / best-effort routes.
2) Soft-demux as the recommended default for paid tiers that need better tail characteristics; enabled behind a runtime flag and on routes with >X p99 complaints historically.
   - Implementation notes: use a conservative burst detector (exponential moving average + short window spike) to avoid thrash. TTL 8–16s worked well in tests.
3) Hard-demux reserved for: enterprise tenants with contractually guaranteed p99 or special low-jitter endpoints. Expose as a configuration knob per-tenant or per-route.
4) Prewarm only for highest-frequency predictable bursts (voice gateway, telephony connectors) — add chargeback line item.

Instrumentation & observability checklist
- Add per-policy breakout in latency/cost dashboards (p50/90/95/99 and slot-hours).
- Burst detector metric: per-session short-window qps and allocated-worker-count.
- Cost attribution: track transient slot allocation time and map to tenant/route for $/1M token model.
- Add synthetic microburst probe (scheduled) to catch regressions in demux routing logic.

Open questions / next experiments
- Multi-model effects: this test used a single model family. Does demux behavior change when mixing heavy/cheap models? Especially if demux pulls a heavy model onto an otherwise light worker.
- Longer bursts: we used 10s bursts. Try 30–120s bursts to evaluate soft-demux TTL and prewarm tradeoffs.
- KV cache crossing: when demux moves a session to a different worker, KV cache miss rate may increase; we disabled KV caching here. Re-run with realistic KV cache to measure combined effects.
- Cost model sensitivity: re-evaluate with reserved capacity pricing (Dedicated) vs on-demand hosted pricing — relative deltas may shift decisions.

Action items (next 2 weeks)
- (Diego) Add per-policy metrics to staging dashboards (INF-3872).
- (Priya) Run variant set: 30s and 90s bursts with soft-demux TTL sweep (6s,12s,24s). Capture p95/p99 and cost delta. (owner: Priya)
- (Anika) Draft a short customer-facing one-pager proposing soft-demux as a default for Pro plans and describing chargeback.
- (Liam) Wire up synthetic microburst probe into QA pipeline to detect regressions.

Notes to reviewers
- This is an engineering cribsheet, not a final vendor-facing benchmark. Numbers should be used to inform product tradeoffs, not quoted in PRs without the full-run artifact.
- Linked artifacts include implementation spike PR and the test harness (see linked_artifacts).
